WF-03 Steps 0.5 and 1 (docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md) for letflow-queue task 107 / GitHub issue #159, claimed via get_next_task. IMPORTANT CONTEXT: this issue was filed by another host mid-run (WF02-REQ043-20260818) while working on REQ-043 (Instance-engine schema: instance_projections ALTER + tasks + tokens tables). That run has NOT merged to main yet in this checkout -- lib/letflow/engine/task.ex does NOT exist here (confirmed: `ls lib/letflow/engine/` shows only instance_state.ex, token.ex, transition.ex from REQ-044, no task.ex). The GitHub issue's body claims 'Local record: docs/issues/ISS-0042.yaml' but that file already exists on main and is a DIFFERENT, unrelated finding (my own REQ-044 run's Graph.t()/CHK-04 type-safety note, already resolved-and-closed) -- this is a cross-host ISS-numbering collision, the same class already documented in docs/anti-patterns.md (ISS-0034/0035, ISS-0036/0037/0039). The correct next available local number on this main is ISS-0043 (highest existing is ISS-0042.yaml).

RAW ISSUE CONTENT (from the queue task, since the local file doesn't exist here to read):
Title: [type-safety] Letflow.Engine.Task.assignee_type is free-text string for a closed USER|GROUP|ROLE set
Body: Found during REQ-043's REVIEWER gate (Step 2d) on lib/letflow/engine/task.ex. Letflow.Engine.Task declares assignee_type as a plain field(:assignee_type, :string) (lib/letflow/engine/task.ex:66), nullable, holding one of exactly three semantic values per EE-03 -- "USER" | "GROUP" | "ROLE" (R-Co's own 005_instances.sql column comment, cited in lib/letflow/design/req043-instance-engine-schema.md section 4.1). The design explicitly considered and declined an Ecto.Enum here ("open free-text per EE-03 section 1a's own column comment; no closed-set validation named by any acceptance criterion") -- a reasoned, in-scope choice, not an oversight. Not a REQ-043 defect and not blocking REQ-043's own REVIEWER PASS. This is a type-safety gap worth tracking: a caller-supplied typo ("Usre", lowercase "user", "Team" instead of "GROUP") is a class of invalid state that today only a runtime query miss or a future test would catch. An Ecto.Enum (values: [:user, :group, :role], stored uppercase to match this table's own established uppercase-status convention, INV-EE43-4) would make the invalid string unrepresentable at the changeset layer instead -- the same pattern already used for tasks.status and tokens.status in this same schema. Filed for whichever future requirement first builds a write path through Letflow.Engine.Task.insert_changeset/2 (REQ-045/051) -- the natural point to add the Ecto.Enum, since it requires no new migration (DB column stays plain :string; only the schema-layer type/cast validation change). Discovered by REVIEWER during WF02-REQ043-20260818.

YOUR JOB: since the actual code isn't visible in this checkout yet, you cannot do a live code-read verification the way the ISS-0042 precedent did (WF03-ISS0042-20260818, see docs/status/requirement_status.yaml and handoffs/registry.json for that precedent's shape). Evaluate this purely on the reasoning presented: is 'defer the Ecto.Enum addition to REQ-045/051, no action needed from this queue task' the correct call, per the issue's own explicit framing and this project's anti-scope-creep norms (CLAUDE.md, core-directives.md)? State explicitly that you could not independently verify against live code and why that's acceptable here (the finding is about a FUTURE write path that doesn't exist yet, not a claim about currently-broken behavior).
acceptance_criteria: Step 0.5 registry lookup: check docs/issues/ for the ISS-0042/ISS-0043-shaped precedent (WF03-ISS0042-20260818) and note the cross-host numbering collision explicitly

Explicit statement that live code verification was not possible (task.ex not merged yet) and why that's acceptable for this specific finding (forward-looking design note, not a current-behavior claim)
Explicit diagnosis: defer (no fix now, correctly scoped to a future requirement) vs. genuine immediate action needed -- state which and why

If deferring: create docs/issues/ISS-0043.yaml (the correct next local number, avoiding the collision) documenting this finding with status: resolved, resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0043-20260818, a resolution_note explaining the diagnosis AND the cross-host numbering-collision correction, github_issue set to the GitHub issue #159 URL. Close GitHub issue #159 via gh issue close 159 --comment explaining both the diagnosis and the local-record renumbering (ISS-0042 -> ISS-0043) for anyone following the GH issue back to this repo. Commit and push on branch fix/WF03-ISS0043-20260818.

result.summary:
Step 0.5 (registry lookup): read docs/issues/ISS-0042.yaml on this branch directly. Confirmed it is the WF03-ISS0042-20260818 precedent for this exact 'diagnosed-and-deferred, no code fix needed' resolution shape (a REVIEWER-filed MINOR type-safety note during a PASSing gate, independently re-verified rather than trusted, concluding a suggested type-level fix is scope creep to add ahead of a requirement/decision record calling for it) -- but also confirmed it is a DIFFERENT, unrelated finding (Letflow.Engine.Transition/Graph.t() CHK-04, from this host's own REQ-044 run), verifying the cross-host ISS-numbering collision the handoff described. `ls docs/issues/` shows ISS-0001..ISS-0042 with no gaps, so ISS-0043 is the correct next available local number; created docs/issues/ISS-0043.yaml fresh at that number rather than overwriting ISS-0042.yaml, matching docs/anti-patterns.md's documented correct handling of this collision class (contrast with the ISS-0036 incident in that file, where a collision was mishandled and overwrote unrelated content).

Step 1 (diagnose): `ls lib/letflow/engine/` in this checkout confirmed only instance_state.ex, token.ex, transition.ex exist (REQ-044's output) -- no task.ex. REQ-043 (which introduces Letflow.Engine.Task) has not merged to main in this checkout; this fix run is itself a concurrent-host artifact of that same unmerged work, so a live code-read verification of lib/letflow/engine/task.ex (as the ISS-0042 precedent performed against transition.ex/graph.ex) was not possible and was not attempted or faked. This is judged acceptable for this specific finding, not a violation of 'reproduce the issue directly': the claim is not about currently-broken runtime behavior reachable by any test or code path today -- it is a forward-looking design-choice observation about a write path (Letflow.Engine.Task.insert_changeset/2) that, per the issue's own text, does not exist yet either ('Filed for whichever future requirement first builds a write path through ... insert_changeset/2 (REQ-045/051)'). There is no failing scenario to run; the artifact the claim rests on is REQ-043's own design doc excerpt quoted verbatim in the issue (req043-instance-engine-schema.md section 4.1: 'open free-text per EE-03 section 1a's own column comment; no closed-set validation named by any acceptance criterion'), and only the *decision recorded there* -- not the design doc's content -- was in question for this diagnosis.

Independent conclusion, reached on the merits rather than by trusting the issue's own recommendation: deferring to REQ-045/051 is correct, not a case needing action now. (1) REQ-043's design doc already treats the open-string choice as reasoned and in-scope, not an oversight -- no current acceptance criterion is violated. (2) No docs/requirements.yaml entry or docs/migration/decisions/ record calls for an Ecto.Enum here today (checked grep for REQ-045/REQ-051 context in docs/requirements.yaml: REQ-045 is the instance-engine execution path that would first build write paths through this schema). (3) Applying CLAUDE.md's and core-directives.md's anti-scope-creep norms directly, and the same reasoning ISS-0042's own resolution applied to its own analogous deferred type-level fix: adding a schema/changeset validation change now, with zero write path yet exercising insert_changeset/2, would be designing ahead of the requirement that actually needs it. (4) ORCHESTRATOR.md section 10's sizing exception does not apply -- this changes cast/validation behavior, not a one-line doc/moduledoc correction (contrast with ISS-0020, which ISS-0042's own precedent noted DID qualify for that exception) -- so even if action were warranted, it would need a full WF-02-shaped chain riding alongside REQ-045/051, not an in-run fix here.
